messages:
alex: quick heads-up — canary v2.3.1 at 5% is showing p95 creepage on response-gen. Not catastrophic but violates our gate (p95 +11%). Can we get a fast root-cause check and a go/no-go? @maria can you run the perf harness and share flamegraphs?

maria: running now. one quick run with `wrk` (defaults, 128conns) 
```
wrk -t4 -c128 -d30s https://canary.example/api/v1/generate
Requests/sec: 1120.45
Latency p50  42.3ms
Latency p95  218.9ms  <-- baseline was ~197ms
Errors: 0
```
seeing a tail bump and a slight increase in std dev. starting perf trace and a `perf` + torchprof capture for the same seed. will share link when uploaded.

tyler: noting distro: this canary picked up the experimental fused-attn kernel (kernel-id: fa-3). we saw small wins on throughput in bench, but maybe it's regressing short-seq lat tails. if maria's trace shows kernel switch thrash we should consider falling back to fa-2.

jen: any customer impact? ops-oncall?

ops-oncall: SLO alert fired for p95 on the canary route 6 minutes ago, no 5xx. traffic is still within burst limits. routed users unaffected for now (5% traffic). filing incident ticket: INC-2025-089.

sre-bot: automatic snapshot: canary:v2.3.1; baseline:v2.3.0; p95_delta:+11.1%; spike_start:2025-05-07T13:04Z; hosts_affected: canary-pool-4 (3/8).

alex: thanks. quick proposal: (1) freeze rollout at 5% (no increase), (2) roll canary back if we confirm kernel thrash, (3) run microbench with `--seq 64 --kv-cache enabled/disabled` to isolate KV cache behavior. any objections?

maria: doing those runs now. first results: KV-cache=on p95 210ms, KV-cache=off p95 224ms. interestingly, enabling cache improved but still above baseline. profile attached: flamegraph link https://artifacts.example/fg/1901234567/ (shows increased time in cudaMemcpy around step 3).

tyler: cudaMemcpy spike suggests memory-copy overhead with the new kernel path — maybe extra staging to host for fused kernel on small batches. that would explain tail. ok to rollback to fa-2 while we iterate.

jen: what's the rollback window? we need to communicate to PMs and support. propose: rollback at +15m if we don't get a fix.

alex: agree. decision: HOLD rollout at 5%. schedule rollback at 13:30 UTC if no mitigations. @maria please try one more run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and also capture nvprof to confirm memcpy origin. if confirmed, tyler and infra can prepare fa-2 rollout.

maria: running now. `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` run: p95 216ms, nvprof shows increased MemcpyHtoD calls clustered at tokens 0-8. upload in 2m.

ops-oncall: prepping rollback playbook: `canary.dsl rollback --service runtime-gen --from v2.3.1 --to v2.3.0 --wait 300s`. will stage the command and hold.

tyler: I'll open PR to pin kernel to fa-2 for the canary pool and create a fast rollback tag. also adding a perf test to catch this pattern (short seq, small batch).

alex: thanks team. action items: maria (confirm nvprof artifact + link), tyler (prep rollback PR + perf test), ops-oncall (standby to execute rollback at 13:30 UTC), jen (PM comms). we'll reconvene in-thread; if anything changes react with :eyes:.
